title: Cambridge 16 · Test 4

sents: The Persians, who lived in present-day Iran, were one of the first civilizations to build tunnels that provided a reliable supply of water to human settlements in dry areas.

In the early first millennium BCE, they introduced the qanat method of tunnel construction, which consisted of placing posts over a hill in a straight line, to ensure that the tunnel kept to its route, and then digging vertical shafts down into the ground at regular intervals.
Underground, workers removed the earth from between the ends of the shafts, creating a tunnel.
The excavated soil was taken up to the surface using the shafts, which also provided ventilation during the work.
Once the tunnel was completed, it allowed water to flow from the top of a hillside down towards a canal, which supplied water for human use.
Remarkably, some qanats built by the Persians 2,700 years ago are still in use today.

paras.conn: ① Ba Tư xây hầm cấp nước → ② phương pháp qanat: cọc, rồi giếng đứng → ③ đào hầm giữa các giếng → ④ đất lên qua giếng, giếng còn thông gió → ⑤ nước chảy ra kênh → ⑥ vẫn còn dùng. Chuỗi: **dân tộc → phương pháp → bước đào → chức năng giếng → kết quả → độ bền**.
paras.main: Người Ba Tư phát minh phương pháp qanat: đặt cọc định hướng, đào giếng đứng và hầm để dẫn nước ra kênh.

sents: They later passed on their knowledge to the Romans, who also used the qanat method to construct water-supply tunnels for agriculture.
Roman qanat tunnels were constructed with vertical shafts dug at intervals of between 30 and 60 meters.
The shafts were equipped with handholds and footholds to help those climbing in and out of them and were covered with a wooden or stone lid.
To ensure that the shafts were vertical, Romans hung a plumb line from a rod placed across the top of each shaft and made sure that the weight at the end of it hung in the center of the shaft.
Plumb lines were also used to measure the depth of the shaft and to determine the slope of the tunnel.

The 5.6-kilometer-long Claudius tunnel, built in 41 CE to drain the Fucine Lake in central Italy, had shafts that were up to 122 meters deep, took 11 years to build and involved approximately 30,000 workers.

paras.conn: ① Ba Tư truyền cho La Mã → ② giếng cách nhau → ③ giếng có chỗ bám và nắp → ④ dây dọi giữ giếng thẳng → ⑤ dây dọi còn đo độ sâu, dốc → ⑥ ví dụ Claudius. Chuỗi: **truyền nghề → cấu trúc → kiểm tra thẳng đứng → ví dụ**.
paras.main: La Mã dùng qanat với giếng có chỗ bám, nắp đậy và dây dọi để giữ thẳng; ví dụ là hầm Claudius.

sents: By the 6th century BCE, a second method of tunnel construction appeared called the counter-excavation method, in which the tunnel was constructed from both ends.
It was used to cut through high mountains when the qanat method was not a practical alternative.
This method required greater planning and advanced knowledge of surveying, mathematics and geometry as both ends of a tunnel had to meet correctly at the center of the mountain.
Adjustments to the direction of the tunnel also had to be made whenever builders encountered geological problems or when it deviated from its set path.
They constantly checked the tunnel's advancing direction, for example, by looking back at the light that penetrated through the tunnel mouth, and made corrections whenever necessary.
Large deviations could happen, and they could result in one end of the tunnel not being usable.

An inscription written on the side of a 428-meter tunnel, built by the Romans as part of the Saldae aqueduct system in modern-day Algeria, describes how the two teams of builders missed each other in the mountain and how the later construction of a lateral link between both corridors corrected the initial error.

paras.conn: ① phương pháp 2: hai đầu → ② khi qanat không thực tế → ③ cần kế hoạch và kiến thức → ④⑤ chỉnh hướng → ⑥ sai lớn thì hỏng một đầu → ⑦ ví dụ Saldae: hai đội trượt nhau, sửa bằng hành lang nối. Chuỗi: **phương pháp → khi dùng → yêu cầu → kiểm tra → rủi ro → ví dụ**.
paras.main: Phương pháp đào từ hai đầu dùng cho núi cao, đòi hỏi kế hoạch kỹ; ví dụ Saldae cho thấy hai đội trượt nhau và phải sửa.
warn: ⚠️ **→ Q7:** `second method` ≠ `replaced`; **→ Q9:** nguồn là **chữ khắc**, không phải sách.

sents: The Romans dug tunnels for their roads using the counter-excavation method, whenever they encountered obstacles such as hills or mountains that were too high for roads to pass over.
An example is the 37-meter-long, 6-meter-high, Furlo Pass Tunnel built in Italy in 69-79 CE.
Remarkably, a modern road still uses this tunnel today.
Tunnels were also built for mineral extraction.
Miners would locate a mineral vein and then pursue it with shafts and tunnels underground.
Traces of such tunnels used to mine gold can still be found at the Dolaucothi mines in Wales.
When the sole purpose of a tunnel was mineral extraction, construction required less planning, as the tunnel route was determined by the mineral vein.

sents: Roman tunnel projects were carefully planned and carried out.
The length of time it took to construct a tunnel depended on the method being used and the type of rock being excavated.
The qanat construction method was usually faster than the counter-excavation method as it was more straightforward.
This was because the mountain could be excavated not only from the tunnel mouths but also from shafts.
The type of rock could also influence construction times.
When the rock was hard, the Romans employed a technique called fire quenching which consisted of heating the rock with fire, and then suddenly cooling it with cold water so that it would crack.
Progress through hard rock could be very slow, and it was not uncommon for tunnels to take years, if not decades, to be built.
Construction marks left on a Roman tunnel in Bologna show that the rate of advance through solid rock was 30 centimeters per day.
In contrast, the rate of advance of the Claudius tunnel can be calculated at 1.4 meters per day.
Most tunnels had inscriptions showing the names of patrons who ordered construction and sometimes the name of the architect.

For example, the 1.4-kilometer Çevlik tunnel in Turkey, built to divert the floodwater threatening the harbor of the ancient city of Seleuceia Pieria, had inscriptions on the entrance, still visible today, that also indicate that the tunnel was started in 69 CE and was completed in 81 CE.

sents: Look around on your next plane trip.
The iPad is the new pacifier for babies and toddlers.
Younger school-aged children read stories on smartphones; older kids don't read at all, but hunch over video games.
Parents and other passengers read on tablets or skim a flotilla of email and news feeds.

Unbeknown to most of us, an invisible, game-changing transformation links everyone in this picture: the neuronal circuit that underlies the brain's ability to read is subtly, rapidly changing and this has implications for everyone from the pre-reading toddler to the expert adult.

simp.text: Everyone on a plane uses screens (children, kids, parents).
Unbeknown to most of us, an invisible transformation links everyone: the neuronal circuit underlying the ability to read is changing, with implications for everyone

paras.main: Mọi người đều dùng màn hình, và điều mà ít ai biết là mạch não dùng để đọc đang âm thầm thay đổi.

sents: As work in neurosciences indicates, the acquisition of literacy necessitated a new circuit in our species' brain more than 6,000 years ago.
That circuit evolved from a very simple mechanism for decoding basic information, like the number of goats in one's herd, to the present, highly elaborated reading brain.

My research depicts how the present reading brain enables the development of some of our most important intellectual and affective processes: internalized knowledge, analogical reasoning, and inference; perspective-taking and empathy; critical analysis and the generation of insight.
Research surfacing in many parts of the world now cautions that each of these essential 'deep reading' processes may be under threat as we move into digital-based modes of reading.

simp.text: Literacy necessitated a new circuit in the brain more than 6,000 years ago.
That circuit evolved from a simple mechanism to the present elaborated reading brain.
The reading brain enables important intellectual and affective processes
simp.note: bỏ liệt kê sau dấu hai chấm

simp.text: Research cautions that these deep reading processes may be under threat as we move into digital reading.

paras.main: Mạch đọc hình thành hơn 6,000 năm và giúp phát triển tư duy sâu, nhưng các quá trình này có thể bị đe dọa khi đọc trên màn hình.

sents: This is not a simple, binary issue of print versus digital reading and technological innovations.
As MIT scholar Sherry Turkle has written, we do not err as a society when we innovate but when we ignore what we disrupt or diminish while innovating.

In this hinge moment between print and digital cultures, society needs to confront what is diminishing in the expert reading circuit, what our children and older students are not developing, and what we can do about it.

simp.text: This is not a simple issue of print versus digital.
We do not err when we innovate but when we ignore what we disrupt or diminish
Society needs to confront what is diminishing in the reading circuit and what we can do about it.

paras.main: Đây không phải chuyện in so với số, mà là cần chú ý điều bị mất đi khi đổi mới và tìm cách xử lý.

sents: We know from research that the reading circuit is not given to human beings through a genetic blueprint like vision or language; it needs an environment to develop.
Further, it will adapt to that environment's requirements - from different writing systems to the characteristics of whatever medium is used.
If the dominant medium advantages processes that are fast, multi-task oriented and well-suited for large volumes of information, like the current digital medium, so will the reading circuit.
As UCLA psychologist Patricia Greenfield writes, the result is that less attention and time will be allocated to slower, time-demanding deep reading processes.

simp.text: The reading circuit is not given by a genetic blueprint; it needs an environment to develop
It will adapt to the environment's requirements
If the dominant medium advantages fast processes, so will the reading circuit.
Less time will be allocated to slower, deep reading.

paras.conn: ① cần môi trường → ② thích nghi theo → ③ môi trường số nên ưu tiên nhanh → ④ ít thời gian cho đọc sâu. Chuỗi: **điều kiện → thích nghi → hệ quả → kết quả**.
paras.main: Mạch đọc không bẩm sinh mà thích nghi với môi trường; môi trường số làm giảm thời gian dành cho đọc sâu.

sents: Increasing reports from educators and from researchers in psychology and the humanities bear this out.

English literature scholar and teacher Mark Edmundson describes how many college students actively avoid the classic literature of the 19th and 20th centuries in favour of something simpler as they no longer have the patience to read longer, denser, more difficult texts.

We should be less concerned with students' 'cognitive impatience', however, than by what may underlie it: the potential inability of large numbers of students to read with a level of critical analysis sufficient to comprehend the complexity of thought and argument found in more demanding texts.

simp.text: Increasing reports bear this out.
Edmundson describes how many college students avoid classic literature in favour of something simpler because they no longer have the patience
We should be less concerned with impatience, however, than with the potential inability to read critically

paras.main: Sinh viên tránh sách kinh điển vì thiếu kiên nhẫn, nhưng đáng lo hơn là khả năng phân tích phê phán bị mất.
warn: ⚠️ **→ Q17:** `less concerned` là ý của **tác giả**, không phải của Edmundson.

sents: Multiple studies show that digital screen use may be causing a variety of troubling downstream effects on reading comprehension in older high school and college students.
In Stavanger, Norway, psychologist Anne Mangen and colleagues studied how high school students comprehend the same material in different mediums.
Mangen's group asked subjects questions about a short story whose plot had universal student appeal; half of the students read the story on a tablet, the other half in paperback.

Results indicated that students who read on print were superior in their comprehension to screen-reading peers, particularly in their ability to sequence detail and reconstruct the plot in chronological order.

simp.text: Digital screen use may be causing troubling effects on reading comprehension
Mangen studied how students comprehend the same material in different mediums.
Half read on a tablet, half in paperback
Print readers were superior in comprehension, particularly in sequencing detail and reconstructing the plot

paras.main: Nghiên cứu của Mangen cho thấy đọc sách in hiểu tốt hơn đọc màn hình, nhất là việc sắp xếp trình tự.

sents: Ziming Liu from San Jose State University has conducted a series of studies which indicate that the 'new norm' in reading is skimming, involving word-spotting and browsing through the text.
Many readers now use a pattern when reading in which they sample the first line and then word-spot through the rest of the text.
When the reading brain skims like this, it reduces time allocated to deep reading processes.
In other words, we don't have time to grasp complexity, to understand another's feelings, to perceive beauty, and to create thoughts of the reader's own.

simp.text: Liu's studies indicate that the new norm in reading is skimming, involving word-spotting
Many readers sample the first line and then word-spot through the rest.
Skimming reduces time allocated to deep reading.
We don't have time to grasp complexity, to understand another's feelings, to perceive beauty

paras.main: Đọc lướt, bắt từ rời rạc đang là thói quen mới, làm giảm thời gian đọc sâu và hiểu cảm xúc.

sents: The possibility that critical analysis, empathy and other deep reading processes could become the unintended 'collateral damage' of our digital culture is not a straightforward binary issue about print versus digital reading.
It is about how we all have begun to read on various mediums and how that changes not only what we read, but also the purposes for which we read.
Nor is it only about the young.
The subtle atrophy of critical analysis and empathy affects us all equally.
It affects our ability to navigate a constant bombardment of information.
It incentivizes a retreat to the most familiar stores of unchecked information, which require and receive no analysis, leaving us susceptible to false information and irrational ideas.

simp.text: The possibility that deep reading could become collateral damage is not a binary issue.
It is about how we read on various mediums and how that changes not only what we read but also why
Nor is it only about the young.
The atrophy of critical analysis affects us all equally
It affects our ability to navigate information.
It incentivizes a retreat to unchecked information, leaving us susceptible to false information

paras.conn: ① không phải in so với số → ② mà là cách ta đọc → ③ không chỉ trẻ → ④ ảnh hưởng đồng đều → ⑤ khả năng xử lý thông tin → ⑥ dễ tin thông tin sai. Chuỗi: **phủ định cách nhìn đơn giản → phạm vi → tác động**.
paras.main: Suy giảm khả năng phân tích và đồng cảm ảnh hưởng tất cả mọi người, khiến ta dễ tin thông tin chưa kiểm chứng.

sents: There's an old rule in neuroscience that does not alter with age: use it or lose it.
It is a very hopeful principle when applied to critical thought in the reading brain because it implies choice.
The story of the changing reading brain is hardly finished.
We possess both the science and the technology to identify and redress the changes in how we read before they become entrenched.
If we work to understand exactly what we will lose, alongside the extraordinary new capacities that the digital world has brought us, there is as much reason for excitement as caution.

simp.text: Use it or lose it.
It is a hopeful principle because it implies choice.
The story of the changing reading brain is hardly finished.
We possess the science and technology to identify and redress the changes before they become entrenched
If we work to understand what we will lose, there is as much reason for excitement as caution.

paras.main: Vẫn còn cơ hội sửa đổi vì ta có khoa học và công nghệ để nhận ra và khắc phục thay đổi trước khi cố định.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

items.q: What is the writer's main point in the first paragraph?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 1):*
> ③④ **Children and adults read on screens.** ⑤ **Unbeknown to most of us, an invisible transformation links everyone: the neuronal circuit underlying the ability to read is subtly, rapidly changing.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | công nghệ đang có **tác động ngầm** lên chúng ta | ✓ `Unbeknown … invisible … transformation` |
| B | công nghệ giúp trẻ **học đọc** | ✗ Không nói |
| C | nên khuyến khích du khách dùng công nghệ trên máy bay | ✗ Máy bay chỉ là **bối cảnh** |
| D | chơi game **phổ biến hơn** đọc | ✗ Chỉ nói một nhóm trẻ |

→ **Đáp án: A**

options.t: Our use of technology is having a hidden effect on us.
Technology can be used to help youngsters to read.
Travellers should be encouraged to use technology on planes.
Playing games is a more popular use of technology than reading.

items.q: What main point does Sherry Turkle make about innovation?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 3②):*
> **We do not err as a society when we innovate but when we ignore what we disrupt or diminish while innovating.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | đổi mới làm **giảm đọc sách in** | ✗ Không phải ý của bà |
| B | cần **chú ý điều có thể mất đi** khi đổi mới | ✓ `ignore what we disrupt or diminish` |
| C | khuyến khích giới trẻ tham gia đổi mới | ✗ |
| D | khác biệt giữa phát triển sản phẩm và ý tưởng | ✗ |

→ **Đáp án: B**

options.t: Technological innovation has led to a reduction in print reading.
We should pay attention to what might be lost when innovation occurs.
We should encourage more young people to become involved in innovation.
There is a difference between developing products and developing ideas.

items.q: What point is the writer making in the fourth paragraph?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 4①–②):*
> **The reading circuit is not given by a genetic blueprint; it needs an environment to develop. It will adapt to the environment's requirements.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | con người có khả năng đọc viết **bẩm sinh** | ✗ Bài nói **ngược** (`not given by a genetic blueprint`) |
| B | đọc bằng **nhiều phương tiện** | ✗ Chỉ là ví dụ |
| C | hệ thống chữ viết đặt yêu cầu **bất ngờ** lên não | ✗ Không nói |
| D | một số mạch não **điều chỉnh theo yêu cầu** | ✓ `will adapt to that environment's requirements` |

→ **Đáp án: D**

options.t: Humans have an inborn ability to read and write.
Reading can be done using many different mediums.
Writing systems make unexpected demands on the brain.
Some brain circuits adjust to whatever is required of them.

items.q: According to Mark Edmundson, the attitude of college students
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 5②):*
> **Many college students actively avoid the classic literature of the 19th and 20th centuries in favour of something simpler as they no longer have the patience to read longer, denser texts.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | thay đổi **cách ông dạy** | ✗ Không nói |
| B | ảnh hưởng đến **họ chọn đọc gì** | ✓ `avoid … in favour of something simpler` |
| C | ông **ít lo** hơn người khác | ✗ Đó là tác giả (5③ `We should be less concerned…`), không phải Edmundson |
| D | không khớp quan điểm công chúng | ✗ Không nói |

→ **Đáp án: B**

⚠️ **C** dễ nhầm vì câu ③ dùng `less concerned`; đó là ý của **tác giả**, câu hỏi hỏi **Edmundson**.

options.t: has changed the way he teaches.
has influenced what they select to read.
does not worry him as much as it does others.
does not match the views of the general public.

groups.instr: Complete the summary using the list of words, A-H, below.

items.q: There have been many studies on digital screen use, showing some ______ trends.
items.exp:
→ tính từ trước `trends`.
> 6① **Digital screen use may be causing a variety of troubling downstream effects.**

`troubling` = **D worrying**.

items.q: Her team then used a question-and-answer technique to find out how ______ each group's understanding of the plot was.
items.exp:
→ tính từ đứng sau `how`.
> 6③–④ **… asked questions about a short story … Results indicated print readers were superior in their comprehension.**

`how ___ understanding was` = mức độ hiểu → **H thorough**.

items.q: The findings showed a clear pattern in the responses, with those who read screens finding the order of information ______ to recall.
items.exp:
→ tính từ + `to recall`.
> 6④ **… particularly in their ability to sequence detail and reconstruct the plot in chronological order.**

Người đọc màn hình **kém** hơn ở việc sắp xếp → `hard to recall` → **F hard**.

items.q: Studies by Ziming Liu show that students are tending to read ______ words and phrases in a text to save time.
items.exp:
→ tính từ.
> 7①–② **Skimming, involving word-spotting … sample the first line and then word-spot through the rest.**

`word-spotting` = đọc **từng từ riêng lẻ** → **B isolated**.

items.q: This approach, she says, gives the reader a superficial understanding of the ______ content of material, leaving no time for thought.
items.exp:
→ tính từ.
> 7④ **We don't have time to grasp complexity, to understand another's feelings, to perceive beauty.**

`another's feelings`, `beauty` = nội dung **cảm xúc** → **C emotional**.

⚠️ **E many** nghe hợp với `words`, nhưng nghĩa Q21 là **rời rạc**; **G combined**, **A fast** không hợp.

options.t: fast
isolated
emotional
worrying
many
hard
combined
thorough

groups.guide: A fast · B isolated · C emotional · D worrying · E many · F hard · G combined · H thorough.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 2?

items.q: The medium we use to read can affect our choice of reading content.
items.exp:
> 8② **It is about how we have begun to read on various mediums and how that changes not only what we read, but also the purposes for which we read.**

`affect our choice of reading content` = `changes … what we read`.

→ **YES**
pairs: affect our choice of reading content

items.q: Some age groups are more likely to lose their complex reading skills than others.
items.exp:
> 8③–④ **Nor is it only about the young. The subtle atrophy … affects us all equally.**

`more likely … than others` ↔ `all equally` → ngược.

→ **NO**

items.q: False information has become more widespread in today's digital era.
items.exp:
> 8⑥ **… leaving us susceptible to false information and irrational ideas.**

Bài nói **dễ bị ảnh hưởng** bởi thông tin sai, **không nói** nó **lan rộng hơn**.

→ **NOT GIVEN**

⚠️ `susceptible to` ≠ `more widespread`: là khả năng bị tác động, không phải số lượng.

items.q: We still have opportunities to rectify the problems that technology is presenting.
items.exp:
> 9④ **We possess both the science and the technology to identify and redress the changes … before they become entrenched.**

`rectify` = `redress`.

→ **YES**

groups.instr: Reading Passage 3 has six sections, A-F. Choose the correct heading for each section from the list of headings below.

items.q: Section A
items.exp:
*The superiority of AI projections over those made by humans*
> ⑤ **AI is almost always better at forecasting than we are.**

`superiority of AI projections` = `better at forecasting`.

items.q: Section B
items.exp:
*Widespread distrust of an AI innovation*
> **Watson for Oncology … doctors ignore the recommendations and stick to their own expertise.**

`AI innovation` = `Watson`; `distrust` = `suspicion and disbelief`.

⚠️ `ii` cũng hợp (lý do tin người hơn), nhưng **B** là **một trường hợp cụ thể**; **C** mới giải thích **lý do chung**.

items.q: Section C 30 Section D
items.exp:
*Reasons why we have more faith in human judgement than in AI*
> ② **Trust in other people is based on understanding how others think.** ④⑤ **AI is new and unfamiliar; its decision-making is too difficult to comprehend.**

`reasons` = nhiều lý do (không hiểu, quen thuộc, truyền thông); `human judgement` ↔ AI.

items.q: Section D
items.exp:
*An increasing divergence of attitudes towards AI*
> ③ **Watching sci-fi films polarised attitudes.** ⑥ **A society split between those who benefit and those who reject.**

`divergence of attitudes` = `polarised`, `split`.

items.q: Section E
items.exp:
*Encouraging openness about how AI functions*
> ④ **Another solution may be to reveal more about the algorithms.** ⑤ **Transparency reports.**

`openness` = `transparency`; `how AI functions` = `algorithms`.

items.q: Section F
items.exp:
*The advantages of involving users in AI processes*
> ② **When people were allowed to slightly modify an algorithm, they felt more satisfied … more likely to use it.**

`involving users` = `allowed … control`.

⚠️ **Tiêu đề thừa:** `iv` (AI giúp ta quyết định tốt) và `viii` (một ứng dụng AI thành công bất ngờ).

options.t: An increasing divergence of attitudes towards AI
Reasons why we have more faith in human judgement than in AI
The superiority of AI projections over those made by humans
The process by which AI can help us make good decisions
The advantages of involving users in AI processes
Widespread distrust of an AI innovation
Encouraging openness about how AI functions
A surprisingly successful AI application

groups.guide:
Ý chính từng phần:

| Phần | Ý chính |
|---|---|
| A | AI dự đoán giỏi hơn người, nhưng người **thiếu tin** và thích chuyên gia người |
| B | Ví dụ Watson for Oncology: bác sĩ **không tin**, bỏ qua |
| C | Lý do người **không tin AI**: không hiểu, lo, truyền thông nhấn mạnh thất bại |
| D | Thái độ về AI **phân cực**, có thể chia rẽ xã hội |
| E | Cách tăng niềm tin: kinh nghiệm, **minh bạch** thuật toán |
| F | Cho người dùng **kiểm soát** thì họ tin hơn |

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

items.q: What is the writer doing in Section A?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (A):*
> ⑥ **Yet we still seem to deeply lack confidence in AI predictions.** ⑦ **People prefer to trust human experts, even if wrong.** ⑧⑨ **We need to understand why people are so reluctant to trust AI.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | đưa ra **giải pháp** cho một mối lo | ✗ Giải pháp ở **E, F** |
| B | **biện minh** cho một ý kiến | ✗ |
| C | **nêu ra** sự tồn tại của **một vấn đề** | ✓ thiếu tin tưởng vào AI |
| D | **giải thích lý do** của hiện tượng | ✗ Lý do ở **C** |

→ **Đáp án: C**

options.t: providing a solution to a concern
justifying an opinion about an issue
highlighting the existence of a problem
explaining the reasons for a phenomenon

items.q: According to Section C, why might some people be reluctant to accept AI?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (C⑤–⑥):*
> **AI's decision-making process is too difficult for most people to comprehend. And interacting with something we don't understand can cause anxiety and give us a sense that we're losing control.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | sợ AI **thay thế con người** trong việc ra quyết định | ✗ Không nói |
| B | **sự phức tạp** khiến họ cảm thấy **yếu thế** | ✓ `too difficult to comprehend` → `losing control` |
| C | muốn **chờ kiểm nghiệm** theo thời gian | ✗ Không nói |
| D | **hiểu sai** làm AI có vẻ **khó hơn thực tế** | ✗ Bài nói nó **thật sự khó hiểu** |

→ **Đáp án: B**

⚠️ **D** đối nghịch tinh tế: bài nói AI **quá khó để hiểu** (khó thật), không phải **hiểu lầm**.

options.t: They are afraid it will replace humans in decision-making jobs.
Its complexity makes them feel that they are at a disadvantage.
They would rather wait for the technology to be tested over a period of time.
Misunderstandings about how it works make it seem more challenging than it is.

items.q: What does the writer say about the media in Section C of the text?
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (C⑨):*
> **Embarrassing AI failures receive a disproportionate amount of media attention, emphasising the message that we cannot rely on technology.**

*Bước 4:*

| | Đáp án | Kết luận |
|---|---|---|
| A | khiến công chúng **mất tin** vào AI | ✓ `emphasising the message that we cannot rely` |
| B | dành **quá nhiều** sự chú ý cho **AI** | ✗ Quá nhiều cho **thất bại** của AI, không phải AI nói chung |
| C | tin về AI thường **không chính xác** | ✗ Không nói |
| D | tạo ấn tượng thất bại do **lỗi người thiết kế** | ✗ Việc người thiết kế mắc lỗi là câu ⑩ riêng |

→ **Đáp án: A**

options.t: It leads the public to be mistrustful of AI.
It devotes an excessive amount of attention to AI.
Its reports of incidents involving AI are often inaccurate.
It gives the impression that AI failures are due to designer error.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3?

items.q: Subjective depictions of AI in sci-fi films make people change their opinions about automation.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (D③–④):*
> **Regardless of whether the film depicted AI positively or negatively, watching it polarised attitudes. Optimists became more extreme, sceptics more guarded.**

*Bước 4:* thái độ **cực đoan hơn** (giữ hướng cũ), **không đổi ý** → ngược.

→ **NO**

items.q: Portrayals of AI in media and entertainment are likely to become more positive.
items.exp:
> D⑥ **As AI is represented more and more in media and entertainment, it could lead to a society split…**

Bài nói AI **xuất hiện nhiều hơn**, không nói **tích cực hơn**.

→ **NOT GIVEN**

items.q: Rejection of the possibilities of AI may have a negative effect on many people's lives.
items.exp:
> D⑦ **Refusing to accept the advantages offered by AI could place a large group of people at a serious disadvantage.**

`rejection` = `refusing to accept`; `negative effect on many` = `serious disadvantage to a large group`.

→ **YES**
pairs: serious disadvantage to a large group

items.q: Familiarity with AI has very little impact on people's attitudes to the technology.
items.exp:
> E② **Simply having previous experience with AI can significantly improve people's opinions.**

`very little impact` ↔ `significantly improve` → ngược.

→ **NO**

items.q: AI applications which users are able to modify are more likely to gain consumer approval.
items.exp:
> F② **When people were allowed the freedom to slightly modify an algorithm, they felt more satisfied with its decisions, more likely to believe it was superior and more likely to use it.**

`gain consumer approval` = `more satisfied`, `more likely to use`.

→ **YES**

exercises.q:
**A. Simplify** – tìm [S]–[V], bỏ phần phụ:
1. `The shafts were equipped with handholds and footholds to help those climbing in and out of them and were covered with a wooden or stone lid.`
2. `We should be less concerned with students' 'cognitive impatience', however, than by what may underlie it: the potential inability of large numbers of students to read with a level of critical analysis sufficient to comprehend the complexity of thought and argument found in more demanding texts.`
3. `On the one hand, if Watson provided guidance that coincided with their own opinions, physicians did not see much point in Watson's recommendations.`

**B. Đại từ:** `This` (P1 đoạn 5④ `This was because…`) chỉ gì? `this` (P2 đoạn 5① `bear this out`) chỉ gì? `this program` (P3 B②) chỉ gì?

**C. Paraphrase:** `troubling` – ? · `rectify` – ? · `rejection` – ? · `openness` – ?

**D.** Vì sao P1 Q7 là **FALSE**?

---
exercises.a:
**A.**
1. [S] The shafts [V] were equipped / were covered (hai vế nối bằng `and`); `to help those climbing…` = mục đích.
2. [S] We [V] should be less concerned with impatience than with the potential inability; vế sau dấu hai chấm là **điều đáng lo hơn**.
3. [S] physicians [V] did not see much point; `if Watson provided…` = điều kiện.

**B.** `This` = **phương pháp qanat nhanh hơn phương pháp hai đầu**; `this` = **việc đọc trên màn hình làm giảm đọc sâu**; `this program` = **Watson for Oncology**.

**C.** `troubling` – `worrying`; `rectify` – `redress`; `rejection` – `refusing to accept`; `openness` – `transparency`.

**D.** Bài nói phương pháp hai đầu là phương pháp **thứ hai** xuất hiện và dùng khi **qanat không thực tế**, nên không thay thế hoàn toàn.

method:
1. **Đọc câu hỏi, xác định cấu trúc** (từ loại ô trống, mắt thông tin).
2. **Định vị** bằng từ không paraphrase được (tên riêng, số, năm).
3. **Simplify** câu trong bài: tìm [S]–[V], bỏ phần phụ.
4. **So ý, không so chữ.**

| Dạng | Nguyên tắc |
|---|---|
| Label the diagram | Đọc **nhãn quanh ô trống** trước (`to direct the tunnelling`, `made of wood or stone`) rồi tìm câu mô tả **bộ phận đó** trong bài |
| T/F/NG, Y/N/NG | Tách câu hỏi thành **mắt thông tin**; FALSE cần chỗ nói **ngược**; NG là **thiếu mắt** |
| Short answer | Từ loại trước; **tối đa hai từ**; lấy **nguyên văn từ bài** |
| Summary với danh sách A–H | **Từ loại trước**, nghĩa sau; mỗi chữ chỉ dùng một lần |
| Matching Headings | Lấy **ý chính cả đoạn**, loại tiêu đề chỉ khớp một chi tiết; có tiêu đề thừa |
| Multiple Choice | Loại từng đáp án bằng lý do cụ thể |
traps:
1. **Từ tuyệt đối** `completely`, `only`, `very little` (Q7, Q8, Q39) → thường FALSE/NO/NG.
2. **Nguồn thông tin:** `inscription` ≠ `ancient book` (Q9).
3. **Ý của ai?** Q17 hỏi **Edmundson**, nhưng `less concerned` là ý **tác giả**.
4. **`susceptible to` ≠ `more widespread`** (Q25) và **`polarised` ≠ `change opinions`** (Q36).
5. **Matching Headings:** phân biệt **ví dụ cụ thể** (B: Watson) với **lý do chung** (C), và loại tiêu đề thừa (`iv`, `viii`).
